summary: Rough, unpolished granite speckled grey, buff and white, as on weathered boulders, kerbs and old building stone.
_comment: Weathered granite: a coarse-grained igneous stone with a rough, unpolished face, its grey, buff and white crystals dulled by the weather (ambientCG Granite003B, CC0, an unpolished 'B' variant; roughness map mean 0.49). The rough sibling of Granite_Polished (Granite001A). Opaque: a solid dielectric; granite does not scatter light through like marble. The source states no physical size: the scan is 0.4 m by a judgement from its grain (crystals of about 3-5 mm), as for Granite_Polished. Made at its tag (Phase19 D-9): the maps are quilted from the scan into an exact 1 m tile at 2048 px (tools/converters/base/quilt_scan.py), every patch at the scan's own size; nothing is stretched. The quilting flattens the scan's broad tone before it quilts (else a broad stain shows as blocks on the patch grid), so the scan's large rust and buff stains are not carried: the weathering reads in the rough, dull face and in the dust and crevice layers. Carries every relevant wear layer at 0 (C1): chipped edge wear (overlay 1, damage) and dust as a deposit (Phase10), gated by the Crevice mask; no third layer is relevant. Not carried: the wet and moss looks the wish list also wants. Built by the Phase11 batch.
name: Granite_Weathered_Clean_Base_s1_v01

sources.why: makes the scan at its scale option: quilted at the scan's own size, never stretched

specular_ior 1.54, that of quartz (Physically Based 'Quartz'), granite's main mineral with feldspar, as on Granite_Polished; Physically Based has no granite entry. The scan's 0.4 m from the grain size, since the source states no physical size; the article tiles at exactly 1 m (quilted).
